user.title: Choose what to set up
user.description: Set up Codex assistants, Voice Match learning, or both as separate entries. Voice learning requires the Voice Match add-on, not a Codex account.

codex.title: Codex Assist
codex.description: Sign in with your ChatGPT/Codex account first. You will choose a chat model from your account’s model list after signing in.

voice_learning.title: Pair Voice Match learning
voice_learning.description: Enable the learning bridge in the add-on's administrator page. Enter its internal HTTP(S) origin and learning key here—not its personalisation key. This verifies pairing only; it does not grant recording consent. When reconfiguring, leave the key blank to keep the existing key.

learning_discovery.title: Choose the Voice Match add-on
learning_discovery.description: These internal addresses came from Home Assistant's cached app metadata. Select one or enter an address manually. A suggestion is not trusted pairing: the next step still requires your separate learning key and an encrypted verification. Nothing will start or record here.

learning_finish.title: Finish learning setup
learning_finish.description:
Encrypted learning pairing was verified. Phone learning: **{phone_status}**.

If enabled, create a separate Voice Learning assistant using both Voice Learning entities from this entry and your usual TTS in [Voice assistants](/config/voice-assistants/assistants). Keep your default assistant unchanged.

Each person needs their own account-assigned profile and separate spoken recording consent. Opening the launcher is not consent. After saving, use Configure → Check setup to verify the assistant. Personal response preferences are a separate optional setup; no Codex account is needed for learning. Submit to save these settings, not to record.

learning_phone.title: Phone voice learning
learning_phone.description: Phone learning is off by default. To enable it, select your ordinary Wyoming Whisper source, not Voice Match's filtered or personalised endpoint. Afterwards, create a separate Voice Learning assistant using both new Voice Learning entities and your usual TTS. Do not change your default assistant. Each account must have its own assigned voice profile and give separate spoken consent.

device.title: Sign in with Codex

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in with Codex again
reauth_confirm.description: Codex Assist needs a fresh ChatGPT/Codex sign-in. Continue to request a new device code.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Codex Assist
reconfigure.description: Sign in again with your ChatGPT/Codex account. Your Codex Assist options will stay unchanged.

model.title: Choose a chat model
model.description: {model_status} Select the model used for Assist conversations and AI Task requests. Availability and feature support can vary by account.

It does not rotate keys, start recording or change Codex. Saving reconfiguration may reload learning and attempt to pause its bound unfinished session; unverified cleanup still needs attention.

confirm.title: Check the dedicated learning assistant
confirm.description: Use both Voice Learning entities from this entry in exactly one dedicated assistant, with your usual TTS. A missing, duplicated or mixed engine pair cannot be selected safely. Keep the default assistant unchanged. Submit continues to a read-only recheck.

confirm.title: Check the launcher without overwriting another panel
confirm.description: The launcher may be missing, or another integration may own /voice-match-learning. Do not overwrite a user panel. Running the old companion and the combined learning module together is not a supported final setup; any cutover needs its own plan and approval. Use manual Assist selection meanwhile. Submit continues to a read-only recheck.

learning_status.title: Learning setup check
learning_status.description:
Learning bridge: **{bridge}**

Whisper source: **{source}**

Learning entities: **{entities}**

Dedicated assistant: **{pipeline}**

Launcher: **{launcher}**

These are technical checks, not profile ownership, recording consent or voice recognition. Correct the relevant settings, then check again. [Voice assistants](/config/voice-assistants/assistants) · [Repairs](/config/repairs). Leave Check again off and Submit to return to the menu.

learning_pairing.title: Repair learning pairing
learning_pairing.description:
On this learning entry, open **Reconfigure** from the entry menu on the [integration page](/config/integrations/integration/codex_assist). Enter the internal origin and learning bridge key; a blank key keeps the existing key. Do not use the personalisation key. An observed bridge problem also offers this route from Repairs.

Reconfiguration reloads only learning and attempts to pause bound unfinished work. It does not delete recordings or change Codex. Unverified cleanup needs attention. Submit returns to this menu without changing anything.

learning_personalisation.title: Choose a Codex entry for personal preferences
learning_personalisation.description: Optional: choose explicitly which existing Codex entry you intend to configure. This guide does not copy keys, change that entry or start Codex sign-in.

learning_personalisation_missing.title: Personal preferences are optional
learning_personalisation_missing.description: No enabled Codex entry is configured. Voice learning works without one. If you want personal response preferences, add Codex assistants separately from the integration module menu, then return here. Nothing has been enabled. Submit returns to the learning menu.

learning_personalisation_guide.title: Set up preferences on the selected Codex entry
learning_personalisation_guide.description:
Pairing status: **{pairing_status}**.

On the [integration page](/config/integrations/integration/codex_assist), open Configure on the Codex entry you selected → Voice Match. Enter the add-on's internal hostname, personalised port (normally 10352) and **personalisation** key, never the learning key. Then select Voice Match with a Codex agent from that entry. Personal instructions are optional; no separate Wyoming Voice Match sources are needed.

This guide cannot verify a key by its shape or prove a received voice packet. Recognition changes response preferences, not HA permissions. Existing personalities, tools and AI Task settings stay unchanged. Submit returns without changing either entry.

learning_phone.title: Phone voice learning
learning_phone.description: Enable only for a dedicated Voice Learning assistant. Use ordinary Wyoming Whisper, not a Voice Match endpoint. Disabling or reloading learning tries to pause its bound unfinished session; unverified cleanup needs attention. It does not delete saved samples or the installed voiceprint. Repair pairing with Reconfigure. Codex settings and your default assistant are unchanged.

mcp.title: MCP servers — read-only preview
mcp.description: Only authenticated HA administrators can use explicitly approved read-only tools. Voice Match grants no access. Native Assist tools are unchanged.

mcp_server.title: MCP connection
mcp_server.description: Use a Streamable HTTP connect URL with a literal IP address (no hostname). Local network access is off by default; enabling it trusts this exact endpoint and permits unencrypted HTTP. Loopback is a separate opt-in for a service on this HA machine, such as the local HA-MCP server. Only enable it for a server you trust; never expose this endpoint publicly without authentication. Metadata addresses and redirects remain blocked. Leave the bearer token blank to keep it; select Clear token to remove it. Saving reloads this integration. Enabling probes tool discovery only; it does not execute tools.

data.id: Stable server ID (lowercase letters, digits, underscore)
data.allow_local: Allow this local network endpoint (HTTP may expose credentials)
data.allow_loopback: Allow loopback endpoint on this Home Assistant machine (required for local HA-MCP)

mcp_tools.title: Connection verified — approve tools
mcp_tools.description: Connected successfully. Found {tool_count} tools declaring themselves read-only. Nothing is approved by default. Review the server's documentation and select only tools you know cannot mutate state or expose unwanted information. Remote annotations are not a security guarantee. Shared server credentials may have administrator access. Approval applies to every assistant for authenticated HA admins only. Changed tool definitions require fresh approval. No writes or Voice Match privileges are supported.

data.confirm_read_only: I verified that these tools are read-only and suitable for HA administrators

voice_match.title: Voice Match
voice_match.description: Connect to the add-on's internal personalised backend (normally port 10352) using its personalisation key, not its learning key. Leave the key blank to keep an existing pairing. Then choose Voice Match in your Codex assistant. No separate Wyoming Voice Match sources are needed. Chat messages stay clean; personal instructions are optional. Saving stops active Voice Match requests. Disabling removes this pairing, not your voices. Recognition is not a login or permission to access private information.

clean_voice.title: Clean voice messages
clean_voice.description: Experimental: keep Voice Match's hidden data out of chat messages. Pair personal preferences first, then choose the personalised Voice Match source (port 10352). After saving, select the new Clean voice messages source in a separate test assistant using a Codex agent from this entry. Keep your usual assistant unchanged. Recognition is not a login. Disabling or changing settings stops active clean-voice requests; it does not delete recordings.

settings.title: Shared AI Task defaults
settings.description:
{model_status}

These settings continue to apply to AI Task. Each conversation assistant has its own settings.

data_description.model: The model used for Assist conversations and AI Task requests.
data_description.text_verbosity: How concise or detailed normal text and voice responses should be.
data_description.web_search: Allow the model to search the web for current information. Search is off by default.

data_description.prompt: Default instructions used for AI Task requests. Conversation agents use their own individual system prompts.
data_description.reasoning_effort: How much reasoning supported models should use before answering.

data_description.image_model: Default quality for images created through Home Assistant AI Task.
data_description.image_size: Default shape and resolution for generated images.

agents.title: Conversation assistants
agents.description: Each assistant has its own personality, model settings, and conversation history. All assistants use this entry’s Codex sign-in and Home Assistant’s exposed-entity controls.

add_agent.title: Add assistant
add_agent.description: Choose a distinct name and personality. The assistant will appear as a conversation agent in Voice assistants.

remove_agent_confirm.title: Confirm assistant removal
remove_agent_confirm.description: Remove {agent_name} from this integration? Any Voice assistant pipeline using it will need another conversation agent.
